SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.34
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by one strong carbonyl stretch at 1660 cm⁻¹, characteristic of an amide C=O (amide-I band).  No second carbonyl band near 1730–1750 cm⁻¹ (ester) or other additional C=O peak is present, so molecules containing two different carbonyl groups (candidates 3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10) are less likely.  The absence of a strong νas(NO₂) band near 1530–1560 cm⁻¹ argues against the nitro-substituted candidate 7.  The intense aliphatic C–H stretches at 2853, 2915 and 2954 cm⁻¹ with only a weak band at 3048 cm⁻¹ fit a molecule that is almost entirely aliphatic and contains several methyl groups; this matches N,N-dimethylacetamide (candidate 1).  Supporting bands for dimethylacetamide reported in Raman spectra include ~1445 cm⁻¹ (CH₃ deformation), ~1370 cm⁻¹ (CH₃ symmetric bend), ~1295 cm⁻¹ (C–N stretch), ~1010 cm⁻¹ (C–C stretch), ~880–900 cm⁻¹ (C–N deformation) and ~580 cm⁻¹ (C–CO bend), all observed here.  The overall pattern of a single amide C=O plus typical aliphatic and C–N bands best matches candidate 1.
